role: PIXL specialist self-review, not independent caller

changes.old_check: The background is transparent: pixels outside the subject have alpha 0 and no opaque matte, box or fringe fills the cell. Partial alpha on subject pixels is permitted; binary alpha is not required.
changes.new_check: The image has transparent negative space outside the designed subject and no unintended opaque canvas matte. Deliberate opaque badge, plate, outline or backing shapes may be part of the subject; authored partial-alpha subject edges or effects are permitted. Judge whether the transparent-background intent is preserved visually, without a binary-alpha or outline-free-glyph rule.
changes.reason: Transparency concerns negative space, not a ban on deliberate subject construction or partial-alpha edges. The old box/fringe wording could reject a valid subject backing or authored edge.

changes.old_check: The dominant colour treatment visibly relates to the existing UI's cool blue accent as seen in assets/start.svg (#70b9ed). This is a visual relationship judgement, not an exact-hex or palette-count rule.
changes.new_check: The image visibly uses the existing UI cool blue accent coherently and perceptibly. The Start fill #70b9ed is a color cue, not an exact palette requirement. The accent need not dominate the subject or occupy a fixed area; a neutral subject with a clear cool-blue accent remains eligible.
changes.reason: BRIEF requires a cool-blue accent, not dominant blue fill. Removing dominant treatment preserves the outcome and permits source-conforming alternatives.

changes.old_check: Composited on #172336, the silhouette is readable at 1x and at 3x nearest-neighbor scale, with no essential detail lost into the panel colour.
changes.new_check: Composited on #172336, the successful-completion check and its asymmetrical arms remain recognizable at native 1x and 3x nearest-neighbor scale. Decorative details may be subtle or disappear if the required semantic silhouette remains readable.
changes.reason: Essential refers to semantic landmarks, not every decoration. #172336 is the consumer display background observation.

changes.old_check: Viewed alone, Ready visibly uses a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion; it reads as completion rather than activity, failure, pause, or the idle Start control.
changes.new_check: Viewed alone, Ready visibly uses a check mark with asymmetrical arms and communicates successful completion. Do not require a specific arm ratio, stroke width, fill dominance, outline or backing recipe. Cross-asset distinctions against Working, Retry and Paused are required later when those assets exist; this sample check does not require those dependent assets.
changes.reason: Keeps the explicit motif and success meaning while separating semantic readability from unavailable family comparison.

changes.old_check: As a representative family sample, the image shows deliberate pixel-art construction: clean pixel clusters and edges, no noisy stray pixels, blur or downscaled-illustration artifacts, and a treatment that could plausibly be extended to Working, Retry and Paused.
changes.new_check: As a representative sample, the image has deliberate pixel-art construction and a plausible reusable treatment for the status family. Assess cluster placement, edges and contrast for the intended 1x/3x display; reject accidental noise or resampling blur that harms the intended treatment. Intentional detached details, authored antialiasing, shading, glows and irregular contours are eligible. Passing this sample-quality check does not approve the family style.
changes.reason: Expert sample-quality criterion, not owner prescription of universally hard edges or connected clusters. It retains the coherent pixel-art outcome.

citation_repairs: All criterion citations now use exact file-local bounded pointers; PHASE supersedes historical OWNER authorization. Historical packet still retained.
art_direction: The retained small asymmetrical check uses compact stepped clusters and a longer rising arm for a clear success landmark. At 16 pixels, silhouette and value separation do more work than surface detail. Existing Start supplies an accent cue, not a pixel-art style approval. Neutral backing and deliberate edge treatment can serve hierarchy while leaving transparent exterior. Choosing this simple blue check as a sample is expert direction, not a universal recipe.

knowledge.silhouette-readability: Native identity landmarks and target background matter; flat masks/multiple backgrounds are optional diagnostics, not source requirements. Fixture proof is bounded.
knowledge.alpha-contract: Alpha policy is separate from palette; compositing acceptance requires a renderer round trip, not just opaque/transparent counts. No binary-alpha requirement here.
knowledge.edge-rhythm: Preserve intentional asymmetry and corners; do not regularize every contour.

observations: Viewed native and enlarged panel views: recognizable short-left/long-right blue check, crisp deliberate steps and strong panel separation. Host delivery dimensions unreported; this is qualitative reassessment, not a new saved full-coverage acceptance.
